headline: Mostly dry and cool with light rain chances Sunday and again Tuesday night into Wednesday, but the big story is a serious risk of moderate to major coastal flooding during Thanksgiving week.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Friday night stays dry and chilly around Glendale and Los Angeles, with a Frost Advisory from midnight to 9 AM Saturday for some colder areas, where temperatures may dip below freezing. North to east winds may turn gusty at times from about 7 PM tonight to 5 AM Saturday, including around Burbank, Van Nuys and LAX and the usual northeast-wind-prone spots, but speeds stay below advisory levels. A passing weak disturbance brought only scattered light showers north of Point Conception (a few hundredths of an inch at most).

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday is dry, and light winds blowing off the land warm things a few degrees, mainly west of the mountains, with highs in the mid to upper 60s and clouds increasing from the northwest through the day. A weak storm brings a decent chance of measurable light rain Sunday through Sunday night, possibly lingering into Monday morning, with totals of a quarter inch or less and no flooding concerns. Highs vary only a little from day to day Sunday and Monday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Another storm crosses the area Tuesday night through Wednesday night, though it does not look very strong. Los Angeles and Ventura counties have lower chances of measurable rain, with around a tenth of an inch or less if any falls, while San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara counties will likely see 0.10–0.50 inch, more near Rocky Butte. Thanksgiving Day and Friday look dry as high pressure builds and light winds blow off the land, with highs in the mid 60s to mid 70s.

coast: Forecasters have significant concern for moderate to major coastal flooding Thanksgiving week, as unusually high sea levels from warm ocean water, extra-high spring tides and a large, long-period west swell combine. For the Central Coast, Ventura and Los Angeles coasts, a Coastal Flood Advisory runs from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM Wednesday (shallow flooding of beach parking lots and low roads, moderate beach erosion), followed by a Coastal Flood Watch from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon, when the swell arrives and significant impacts seem probable. Peak high tides come between about 8:45 and 10 AM, around 8.2–8.6 feet for LA and Ventura and 7.9–8.2 feet on the Central Coast, with a reasonable worst case 0.3–0.5 foot higher; if upgraded to a warning, flooding could reach farther inland and damage coastal roads and buildings. Areas of greatest concern include Santa Monica to Palos Verdes and Long Beach/Naples in LA County; Faria to Silver Strand Beach, inside harbors and Ventura Harbor in Ventura County; and Morro Bay, Pismo Beach, Oceano Dunes and the Cayucos, Avila and Pismo piers. The Santa Barbara South Coast (Santa Barbara to Rincon, plus Jalama Beach) and Catalina and the Channel Islands are under a Coastal Flood Advisory from 3 AM Monday to 3 PM Thursday, with elevated to high surf likely all week and more alerts likely for Friday. Officials advise heeding local authorities, protecting flood-prone property with sandbags or barriers, and staying off rock jetties and flooded roads and walkways. Offshore, Small Craft Advisory winds continue until 3 AM Saturday for the waters south of Point Sal; a front crossing the coastal waters Sunday into Monday could bring isolated to scattered heavy showers, and another front around Wednesday brings wind and rain mainly off the Central Coast, with small-craft-level northwest to west winds possible south of Point Conception Wednesday and Wednesday night and a significant west swell of about 14–16 feet midweek.
watch_for: Coastal flooding Wednesday–Thursday: the watch could be upgraded to a Coastal Flood Warning as the big swell meets peak morning high tides around 8.2–8.6 feet in LA and Ventura.
Frost early Saturday morning in colder areas under the Frost Advisory.
The Tuesday night–Wednesday night storm: likely light rain on the Central Coast, less certain and lighter (0.10 inch or less) for LA and Ventura counties.
confidence: Forecasters say models agree well through both the short and long term, with the main uncertainty being exactly how the swell and high tides line up midweek for coastal flooding.
